business_description: eBay Inc. operates a global online marketplace that connects buyers and sellers across new, used, refurbished, collectible, and hard-to-find goods. The company’s platform supports consumer-to-consumer and business-to-consumer commerce, with meaningful exposure to categories such as parts and accessories, collectibles, fashion, electronics, home and garden, and refurbished goods. eBay’s economics are primarily marketplace-based: it facilitates transactions rather than owning most inventory, generating revenue from transaction fees, seller services, payments-related fees, and advertising products.
business_model: eBay is an asset-light, two-sided marketplace business. Sellers list inventory on the platform and pay fees when items are listed, sold, promoted, or supported by seller tools; buyers use the marketplace to discover and purchase goods. The model depends on marketplace liquidity, buyer traffic, seller supply, trust and safety, search/recommendation quality, payments functionality, and category-specific vertical experiences. Because eBay generally does not take inventory risk for third-party marketplace sales, gross margins can be structurally high, while profitability is driven by GMV, take rate, advertising penetration, operating expense discipline, payment/fraud costs, technology investment, and marketing efficiency.

segments.name: Marketplace
segments.description: Core global marketplace connecting buyers and sellers across consumer goods, collectibles, parts, refurbished items, and other categories. Revenue is primarily generated from final value fees, listing fees, and other transaction-related fees tied to gross merchandise volume.
key_drivers: Category mix and vertical focus areas
Search quality, recommendations, and conversion rates
Seller inventory depth and pricing competitiveness
Cross-border trade and international marketplace activity

segments.name: Advertising and Promoted Listings
segments.description: Advertising products that allow sellers and brands to promote listings and improve visibility within eBay’s marketplace. Revenue is tied to seller adoption, ad pricing, traffic, conversion, and the competitiveness of marketplace categories.

segments.name: Seller Services, Subscriptions, and Payments-Related Services
segments.description: Seller-facing tools and services such as store subscriptions, listing upgrades, managed payments-related fees, and other platform capabilities that help sellers transact and manage their businesses on eBay.
key_drivers: Payments volume and payment processing economics
Regulatory and compliance requirements for payments

macro_sensitivities: Consumer discretionary spending affects GMV, especially in categories such as electronics, fashion, home goods, collectibles, and auto parts
Consumer confidence and household income influence discretionary purchase frequency and average order value
Interest rates and credit conditions can affect demand for higher-ticket discretionary items and small seller business health
FX translation and cross-border trade flows are important because eBay operates globally and reports in U.S. dollars
Shipping costs, fuel prices, and carrier service levels influence seller economics, buyer conversion, and marketplace competitiveness
Digital advertising budgets and seller ROI expectations affect promoted listings and marketplace ad revenue
Competitive pricing pressure from large marketplaces and value-commerce platforms can influence traffic, conversion, and seller retention
Regulation of online marketplaces, payments, data privacy, consumer protection, taxation, counterfeit goods, and platform liability can affect compliance costs and operating flexibility
Labor market and technology wage inflation can affect product development, trust and safety, and customer support costs
major_risks: Intense competition from large e-commerce platforms, vertical marketplaces, social commerce, value-commerce platforms, and direct-to-consumer channels
Declines in active buyers, active sellers, marketplace traffic, or GMV could reduce transaction revenue and weaken network effects
Seller churn or reduced seller economics due to fees, advertising costs, shipping costs, policy changes, or competitive alternatives
Trust and safety failures, counterfeit goods, fraud, chargebacks, account takeovers, or poor buyer experiences could damage marketplace reputation
Search, discovery, and recommendation underperformance could reduce conversion and seller returns
Regulatory and legal risks related to payments, marketplace liability, data privacy, consumer protection, tax collection, sanctions, and counterfeit or prohibited goods
Cybersecurity incidents, system outages, data breaches, or payment disruptions could impair operations and user trust
FX volatility and international regulatory complexity could pressure reported revenue and margins
Advertising monetization risk if ad load hurts buyer experience or sellers reduce promoted listings spend due to weak returns
Execution risk around product modernization, AI adoption, category focus, authentication programs, and buyer/seller experience improvements
